title: Hall conductance of dilute electrolytes from odd stochastic density functional theory
authors: Yael Avni, Michel Fruchart, David Martin, Tali Khain, Vincenzo Vitelli
abstract: Electrolytes under an external magnetic field exhibit a Hall conductivity, much like metals and semiconductors. However, existing theories fail to quantitatively account for their measured Hall conductivities. To make progress toward such a theory, we develop a stochastic density functional framework for electrolytes in a magnetic field. This framework, which we dub odd SDFT, extends the celebrated stochastic density functional theory (SDFT) to incorporate transverse mobilities and chiral time-correlated noise. Using this framework, we calculate the Hall conductivity in the absence of hydrodynamic solvent effects through three approaches: (i) direct response, (ii) Green-Kubo relation, and (iii) a hybrid fluctuation-dissipation relation. We further show that odd SDFT applies more broadly to fluids with broken time-reversal and mirror symmetry, including odd-diffusive fluids and chiral active matter. Our results generalize the relaxation correction of Debye-Hückel-Onsager theory to magnetized electrolytes and provide a foundation for incorporating additional effects mediated by the solvent that could quantitatively reconcile theory and experiments.
summary: This paper develops odd Stochastic Density Functional Theory (odd SDFT) to calculate the Hall conductivity of electrolytes in a magnetic field. By extending standard SDFT, the authors derive a generalized field equation, the odd Dean-Kawasaki equation, which successfully predicts the Hall conductivity. This work provides a robust theoretical foundation for understanding charge transport in complex, magnetized fluid systems.
main_problem: The paper aims to develop a quantitative theory for the Hall conductivity of dilute electrolytes subjected to an external magnetic field, addressing failures in existing theoretical models.
main_result: The authors introduce and utilize odd Stochastic Density Functional Theory (odd SDFT) to calculate the Hall conductivity, showing consistency across three different theoretical approaches.
method: The methodology involves deriving a field theory description, specifically the 'odd Dean-Kawasaki equation,' from an underdamped Langevin equation, and calculating transport coefficients using direct response, Green-Kubo, and fluctuation-dissipation relations.
model_or_system: The system modeled is a dilute electrolyte (charged particles) immersed in a fluid and subjected to an external magnetic field. The dynamics are governed by an underdamped Langevin equation incorporating Lorentz forces and stochastic noise.
key_observables: Hall conductivity ($\kappa_H$); the density and momentum field equations.
important_parameters: The dimensionless parameter $\omega_c	au = qB/\gamma$; the low mass limit ($m 	o 0$); and the magnetic field strength ($B$).
main_assumptions: The primary assumptions include taking the low mass limit ($m 	o 0$) while keeping $\omega_c	au$ fixed, and neglecting fluid advection and the full dielectric response interaction.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically illustrates the low mass limit, contrasting solvent interaction with the magnetic field's cyclotron period. Figure 2 summarizes the derivation path from inertial dynamics to the final odd Dean-Kawasaki equation.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by establishing the underlying Langevin dynamics, deriving the field equations for density and momentum (leading to the odd Dean-Kawasaki equation), and finally applying this framework to calculate the Hall conductivity using multiple theoretical routes, culminating in numerical validation against prior work.
why_interesting: While focused on classical electrochemistry, the use of stochastic density functional theory and the derivation of a generalized, non-equilibrium field equation (odd Dean-Kawasaki) provides a powerful, systematic theoretical framework for systems driven by external fields and noise, which has parallels in open quantum systems dynamics.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Schematic drawing of the low mass limit with explicit and implicit solvent. (a) A particle interacting with solvent molecules (top) with characteristic relaxation time τ much smaller than any other relevant time scale can be described by an effective bath (bottom) with random kicks represented by white noise. (b) A magnetic field introduces an additional time scale: the period of the cyclotron orbit, ∼ω−1 c . If τ and ω−1 c are both much smaller than any other relevant time scale, but their ratio is finite, the particle’s bath has nonwhite noise with traces of chirality (bottom).
